name: Prize crossword No 26,280
preamble: To mark the 60th anniversary of the death of 24. All across clues lack a definition; the solution to one of them indicates what links all the others.

clue.text: Home thus dealt with psychosis, removing a nightly problem?

indicators.note: to remove is to take away, so a letter is taken out of the word before it

blocks.note: someone at home is said to be in
thus and so both mean in this way
mania is a mental disorder
the letter taken out of mania

explanation.surface: A household cures its own mental illness and so gets rid of a sleeping trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dealt with' reads as cured, but it only joins the pieces; the question mark flags that the definition is a loose description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is the inability to sleep, a condition that strikes at night time.

clue.text: Soak up drink and talk too freely?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: to sog is a dialect word for to soak or saturate
to sip is to drink a little

explanation.surface: Someone drinks heavily and then their tongue runs loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak up' reads like one verb meaning absorb, but 'up' is the reversal signal for SOG, a rare word for soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To gossip is to chatter idly about other people's private affairs, saying more than one ought.

clue.text: Little pile of soil? Briefly come out with straw

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut short by its final letter
out can mean wrong or not in order, so the letters are put in a new arrangement

blocks.note: come without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small heap of earth, and an invitation to emerge carrying some hay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come out' looks like a phrase meaning emerge, but 'out' belongs to the anagram and 'come' is shortened to COM.
explanation.definitionFit: A worm cast is the little coil of earth an earthworm leaves on the surface after passing it through its gut.

clue.text: On-the-up Irish singer in Italian city district

indicators.note: in a down entry, something on the up reads from the bottom, so backwards

blocks.note: IR is the abbreviation for Irish
an alto sings in the range below soprano

explanation.surface: A rising Irish star performs in a district of an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On-the-up' sounds like praise for a singer's career but flips only the IR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the old commercial quarter of Venice, famous for its bridge over the Grand Canal.

clue.text: Worker in firm first to retire

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it
the first of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: CO is short for company, a firm
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker
the opening letter of retire

explanation.surface: An employee at a company is the first to take retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: Across clues have no definition here: Georg Cantor, founder of set theory, is one of the mathematicians linked by 13 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Cantor was the German who created set theory and showed that some infinities are larger than others.

clue.text: Cable meeting with journalist is flattered

blocks.note: coax is short for coaxial cable
ED is short for editor, the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A telegram arrives as a reporter is buttered up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cable' suggests a telegram, but here it is the coaxial wire used for TV signals.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax someone is to persuade them gently with soft words, so coaxed and flattered share the sense of sweet-talked.

clue.text: Crowd is hanging round front of university

indicators.note: to hang round something is to surround it, so one piece goes around another
the front of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a mob is an unruly crowd
taken as written
the opening letter of university

explanation.surface: A throng loiters outside the entrance to a university.
explanation.walkthrough: Across clues have no definition: August Möbius, of the one-sided Möbius strip, is one of the mathematicians.
explanation.definitionFit: August Möbius was a German geometer whose name survives in the twisted one-sided band, the Möbius strip.

clue.text: It's hard work getting a new set of punchy words

blocks.note: a slog is a long tiring effort
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A copywriter grumbles that coming up with a fresh catchphrase is a grind.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like a complaint about writing, but simply strings three pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a short memorable phrase used in advertising or campaigning, made to hit hard.

clue.text: Theme worked out with art and wit? Brainy stuff

indicators.note: something worked out has been processed and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An essay topic developed with skill and humour makes for clever reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brainy' looks like it means intellectual, but it is meant literally: stuff the brain is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: White matter is the pale nerve tissue of the brain and spinal cord, made of insulated nerve fibres.

clue.text: I love being embraced by slovenly woman, rolling over

indicators.note: whatever is embraced is held within arms, so one piece sits inside another
something rolling over turns end to end, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: slag is a derogatory British word for a slovenly or promiscuous woman
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A man declares his love while being hugged by a slatternly woman who is turning over.
explanation.walkthrough: IO goes inside SLAG after the S, making SIOLAG, which is then read backwards. Évariste Galois is one of the mathematicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Évariste Galois was a French prodigy who founded group theory before dying in a duel aged twenty.

clue.text: Expression of surprise when meeting poet?

blocks.note: ha is an exclamation of surprise
John Milton, author of Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: Someone gasps on being introduced to a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: With no definition across, the answer is William Rowan Hamilton, the Irish mathematician who invented quaternions.
explanation.definitionFit: William Rowan Hamilton was an Irish mathematician famous for quaternions and his reformulation of mechanics.

clue.text: Cleric's title put in front of name

blocks.note: Ven. is short for Venerable, the title of an archdeacon
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A churchman's honorific is placed before his name.
explanation.walkthrough: John Venn, of the overlapping-circle diagrams, is one of the mathematicians; fittingly he was also a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: John Venn was an English logician whose overlapping circles for showing sets are named Venn diagrams.

clue.text: Cleese, Idle et al, legless around old marketplace

indicators.note: without a leg means one particular piece has been removed
to go around something is to enclose it

blocks.note: John Cleese and Eric Idle were members of the Monty Python comedy team
the agora was the public square and market of an ancient Greek city

explanation.surface: The Monty Python team, blind drunk, stumble around an ancient market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legless' is British slang for very drunk, but here it removes ON, the cricket term for the leg side, from PYTHONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pythagoras was the ancient Greek mathematician whose theorem relates the sides of a right-angled triangle.

clue.text: Dull chemist in difficulty penning article

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as animals in a fold, so one piece goes inside another
something in difficulty is in a mess, so its letters are disordered

blocks.note: mat, or matt, means without shine
taken as written
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A boring pharmacist in trouble writes an essay.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the across answer the preamble mentions: it names what links all the other across solutions, each a mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: Every other across solution is a famous practitioner of this subject, the science of number, quantity and space.

clue.text: Keeping a facility for large-scale ads

blocks.note: first meaning: storing things away and holding on to them
second meaning: a large outdoor board for posters

explanation.surface: Someone retains a site for putting up big advertisements.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a hoarding is what Americans call a billboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoarding means amassing and keeping things, and as a noun is a big board for displaying posters.

clue.text: Around sailor crew is moving sideways

indicators.note: to be around something is to surround it
letters that are moving shift out of their original positions

blocks.note: taken as written
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the crossword's usual sailor

explanation.surface: A ship's company gathers round one seaman as it shifts sideways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is moving' reads as the verb of the sentence, but 'is' joins the anagram fodder and only 'moving' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs scuttle to the side rather than forward, so moving crabwise means going sideways or indirectly.

clue.text: Strip club of sleazy nature on street

blocks.note: a dive is a seedy bar or nightclub
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A seedy strip club sits on a city street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip club' reads as one phrase, but 'Strip' is the definition and 'club' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest is to deprive or strip someone of something, such as clothing, rights or property.

clue.text: Start to find "black gold" under playing field

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece placed under another is written below it, so it comes second

blocks.note: the rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public playing field
black gold is a nickname for crude oil

explanation.surface: Prospectors begin hunting for oil beneath a sports pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' looks like begin, but it means a sudden jump of fright.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to flinch in surprise, and to recoil is to jerk back in fear or disgust.

clue.text: Host unpaid for working

indicators.note: something working is in operation and being changed, so its letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone throws a party without any payment for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: With no definition across, the anagram must produce a mathematician: Diophantus of Alexandria.
explanation.definitionFit: Diophantus of Alexandria was an ancient Greek algebraist; equations with whole-number solutions are named Diophantine after him.

clue.text: Favourite lines about love in this, maybe?

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it on all sides

blocks.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: Treasured verses about romance are what you might find here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' looks like lines of verse, but it is railway lines. The definition points at the clue itself: favourite lines about love might well be in a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasured lines about romance are typically found in verse, so 'this' stands for the literary form they belong to.

clue.text: Yellow orb over county incompletely visible — as it becomes this?

definitions.text: Yellow orb over county incompletely visible — as it becomes this?

indicators.note: something incomplete is missing a part, here its last letter
in a down entry, one piece over another simply comes first

blocks.note: the sun is the yellow ball in the sky
Kent, a county in south-east England, without its last letter

explanation.surface: The setting sun over Kent is only partly visible as it goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue paints the picture of the answer: a sun only partly visible over the horizon has sunk below it.
explanation.definitionFit: A setting sun half below the horizon has dropped down out of sight, which is what sunken describes.

clue.text: Old tower losing its facing

indicators.note: the facing of something is its front surface, so the opening letter goes

blocks.note: the Tower of Babel in the Book of Genesis

explanation.surface: An ancient tower has lost its outer cladding.
explanation.walkthrough: Without its first letter the biblical tower becomes Niels Henrik Abel, the Norwegian mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: Niels Henrik Abel was a Norwegian who proved the general quintic equation cannot be solved by radicals.

clue.text: Very famous bunch of engineers

blocks.note: legend is informal for extremely famous
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A celebrated team of engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: With no definition across, the answer is Adrien-Marie Legendre, the French mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrien-Marie Legendre was a French mathematician known for Legendre polynomials and work on number theory.

clue.text: The latest fashion

blocks.note: the latest thing is the new one
the ton is an old word for fashionable style or society

explanation.surface: Whatever is currently in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The latest fashion' reads as one phrase, but splits into two pieces; Isaac Newton is the mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton co-invented calculus and set out the laws of motion and universal gravitation.

clue.text: On a trip missing nothing

indicators.note: whatever is missing has been left out of the word

blocks.note: someone on a trip is touring
nothing is zero, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone travelling has left nothing behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble names 24 as the man whose death the puzzle marks: Alan Turing, who died in 1954.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Turing was the British mathematician who founded computer science and helped break the Enigma code.

clue.text: Not completely happy, learner being pushed to the back

indicators.note: something not complete is missing its final part
pushed to the back means moved to the end, placed after everything else

blocks.note: blessed, meaning fortunate or happy, without its last letter
L is for learner, as on learner drivers' plates

explanation.surface: A student driver is only partly content at being shoved to the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: The L already in BLESSE moves to the end, giving Friedrich Bessel, the German astronomer and mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Bessel was a German astronomer and mathematician whose Bessel functions appear throughout physics.
